Architecture Diagram

The solution is a single ASP.NET Web Forms application for managing a product catalog. It runs in IIS and can use SQL Server, Azure Blob Storage, OpenID Connect, and Application Insights when configured.

Data Storage & External Services

SQL Server is the configured relational store. The application can instead use an in-memory mock catalog; image storage similarly switches between a mock implementation and Azure Blob Storage. OpenID Connect, Key Vault configuration, and Application Insights are optional integrations controlled by configuration.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • One Web Forms application owns presentation, catalog logic, and persistence; no independently deployed application services were found.
  • Autofac registers the SQL-backed or mock catalog and Azure-backed or mock image services.
  • Entity Framework 6 maps the catalog entities to SQL Server tables and uses database sequences for generated catalog IDs.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are service-level domain/entity classes used by the rendered pages; they are not immutable API DTOs. The upload method serializes an anonymous JSON contract containing name and url using JavaScriptSerializer. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL contract was found.

Communication Patterns

Web Forms pages call ICatalogService and IImageService directly within the same process. Catalog operations use EF6 and SQL Server; image storage uses the configured Azure Blob implementation or a mock implementation. The ASMX upload method is synchronous from the client’s perspective, while blob operations include asynchronous Azure SDK APIs internally. No broker, service discovery, gateway, retry policy, circuit breaker, or cross-service aggregation was identified.

Azure Active Directory OpenID Connect and cookie authentication are enabled conditionally by configuration; otherwise a custom OWIN middleware is used. The inspected page handlers do not show a common explicit role or resource-authorization policy. TLS enforcement is not established by the application source; the supplied local Compose URL uses HTTP.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports maintaining and browsing an e-commerce product catalog. Staff can create, edit, view, and delete catalog items, while optional image-upload support stores product images separately from catalog records.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog managementProduct description, price, image reference, and inventory thresholdsBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalog managementBrand classification for productsCan classify many CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalog managementProduct type classificationCan classify many CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedWebFormsCatalog managementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server; optional Azure Blob Storage

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse catalog

  1. A visitor opens the default page or a paginated catalog route.
  2. The page asks ICatalogService for a page of catalog items; the SQL-backed service loads brand and type relationships, while mock mode reads the in-memory catalog.
  3. The application renders the catalog and image references.

Workflow 2: Create or update a catalog item

  1. A staff user opens the create or edit page; when Azure AD integration is enabled, the page issues an OpenID Connect challenge for an unauthenticated request.
  2. The page validates its model state and builds a CatalogItem from submitted form values.
  3. For an uploaded image, the page finalizes the temporary image through IImageService.
  4. ICatalogService assigns an ID on creation, persists changes through EF6, and redirects to the catalog.

Workflow 3: Upload a catalog image

  1. The browser posts a multipart image to PicUploader.UploadImage.
  2. The method checks that the uploaded content can be decoded as JPEG, PNG, or GIF.
  3. The selected image service stores the temporary image and returns its name and URL as JSON.
  4. During create or edit, the final image is associated with the catalog item.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service catalog aggregation was identified. Catalog data is stored in the application’s SQL Server database; images are stored through Azure Blob Storage only when enabled, otherwise mock storage is selected. There is no application-level fallback or compensation documented for a partially completed catalog save and blob update.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Staff participant Page as "Catalog page" participant Catalog as "Catalog service" participant DB as "SQL Server or mock catalog" participant Image as "Image service" participant Storage as "Azure Blob or mock storage" Staff->>Page: Submit catalog item Page->>Page: Validate model state alt Validation succeeds opt Image supplied Staff->>Page: Upload image Page->>Image: Validate image format and store temporary image Image->>Storage: Store temporary image when enabled Storage-->>Image: Temporary image reference Image-->>Page: Image name and URL end Page->>Catalog: Create or update item Catalog->>DB: Assign ID and save catalog changes DB-->>Catalog: Save result opt Image supplied Page->>Image: Finalize image reference Image->>Storage: Copy to item location when enabled Storage-->>Image: Final image result end Catalog-->>Page: Operation complete Page-->>Staff: Redirect to catalog else Validation fails Page-->>Staff: Redisplay form with validation errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item prices must be non-negative and use at most two decimal places; stock, restock, and maximum-stock values have non-negative bounded ranges.
  • Each catalog item requires a brand and type relationship. Item IDs are allocated with a SQL sequence-backed hi-lo generator.
  • Image upload accepts decoded JPEG, PNG, and GIF content. The image-upload service stores the temporary file before a catalog update is finalized.
  • Catalog initialization runs SQL sequence scripts and seeds brands, types, and items from built-in defaults or optional CSV customization data.
  • Mutations are saved with EF6 SaveChanges; no explicit cross-resource transaction or compensation across SQL and blob storage was identified.
  • No personal, health, or payment data is represented by the catalog domain entities.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses the legacy packages.config format. Entity Framework 6.3.0, OWIN, and several Azure integration packages are older generations; compatibility and support should be checked when upgrading the application platform.

The catalog data layer contains three EF6 entities stored in SQL Server. The application uses one catalog database, with optional mock data for local runs.

Entity Model

erDiagram CatalogBrand ||--o{ CatalogItem : "categorizes" CatalogType ||--o{ CatalogItem : "classifies" CatalogItem { int Id PK string Name string Description decimal Price string PictureFileName int CatalogTypeId FK int CatalogBrandId FK int AvailableStock int RestockThreshold int MaxStockThreshold bool OnReorder } CatalogBrand { int Id PK string Brand } CatalogType { int Id PK string Type }

CatalogItem is mapped to the Catalog table and has required foreign keys to the brand and type tables. PictureUri and TempImageName are ignored by EF. The mappings and keys are configured in Models/CatalogDBContext.cs; the entity declarations are in Models/CatalogItem.cs, Models/CatalogBrand.cs, and Models/CatalogType.cs.

Caching Strategy

No application-level or EF query cache was identified. CatalogServiceMock keeps an in-memory mutable list when mock mode is enabled; this is the mock data source, not a cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

One Web Forms application accesses the catalog database directly through EF6. There are no separate service-owned stores, cross-service database reads, CQRS projections, or messaging-based data flows. SQL sequence scripts are executed during database initialization; catalog types, brands, and items are seeded from built-in data or optional CSV files.
